Suru and Naru

Two very common verbs for describing change are Suru (to do/make) and Naru (to become).

Naru (To Become)

Used with the particle ni (for nouns/na-adj) or ku (for i-adj).

With Nouns / Na-adjectives

先生になる。(Sensei ni naru.) (Become a teacher.)\nきれいになる。(Kirei ni naru.) (Become pretty/clean.)

With I-adjectives

Drop the i and add ku. 熱くなる。(Atsuku naru.) (Become hot.)

Suru (To Make / Decide)

Used similarly with ni or ku to mean making something act in that way, or deciding on something.

“To Make”

部屋をきれいにする。(Heya wo kirei ni suru.) (Make the room clean.)\n音を大きくする。(Oto wo okiku suru.) (Make the sound louder.)

“To Decide on”

これにします。(Kore ni shimasu.) (I will decide on this one. [Ordering at a restaurant])
